title: Quotient data before local elimination in desingularization
statement: Let R be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], Λ an R-algebra, A a finitely presented R-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], π∈R, and α:A→Λ an R-algebra map. Assume Ann_Λ(π)=Ann_Λ(π²), the image of π in A is strictly standard [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element], and there is an R-algebra section ρ:A/π⁴A→R/π⁴R compatible with α modulo π⁴. Then there is a finitely presented R-algebra S and an ideal K of S such that K⊆(π²), (π)K⊆K², and S/K is finitely presented. There are R-algebra maps aB:A→S/K and β:S/K→Λ with β∘aB=α. The principal localization (S/K)_π is smooth over R. At every prime p of S containing π, R→S is smooth at p [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] and S_p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is flat over R [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. The conclusion does not assert any smoothness of S/K at primes containing π.

source.place: Stacks Project, Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CR (lemma-desingularize)

proof.text: Apply the polynomial substitution construction to obtain a presentation P, the polynomials xi,F,g,e, and the evaluation coefficients. This is steps 1-5 and the ideal-square observation of the original plan.

Construct S=Q/(g) and K as the image of (F). Finite polynomial variable and relation families give finite presentation of S and S/K. Apply Ideal.map to (F)⊆(pi^2) and (pi)(F)⊆(g)+(F)^2 to prove K⊆(pi^2) and (pi)K⊆K^2. The map from the presentation polynomial ring to S/K kills all relations, hence descends along its surjection to a map aB:A→S/K.

Evaluate v at zero and w_i at pi lambda_i. This sends xi_i to alpha(P.val_i), and therefore kills each F_j. For j<c, pi^3 times the evaluation of g_j is zero. The affine formula for g_j shows that its evaluation is pi times an explicit element t. Apply Ann(pi)=Ann(pi^2) successively to t pi^2, t pi, and t to reduce t pi^4=0 to t pi=0. Evaluation consequently kills both (g) and K, so descends to beta:S/K→Lambda. Check beta aB=alpha on the surjective presentation map.

The inverted quotient is A_pi[v] by the inverted-quotient equivalence. Strictly standard localization is smooth; a finite polynomial ring is smooth; smoothness composes and transports along the inverse R-algebra equivalence. This proves (S/K)_pi is smooth.

At a prime q of S containing pi, use the naive pre-submersive presentation of S with selected v variables. After quotienting by q, its derivative matrix is the identity, since g_j=v_j+sum r_ji w_i+pi e_j. Its determinant d therefore avoids q. Compose this presentation with the standard presentation of localization at d. Its Jacobian is the product of the two unit images of d, so Mathlib gives standard smoothness, hence smoothness of S_d. This directly witnesses IsSmoothAtPrime R q, including c=0. Smooth algebras are flat. Regard S_q as the further localization of S_d, since powers of d lie in the prime complement; localization is flat, and transitivity proves Module.Flat R S_q. This replaces the fibre-dimension route below the unit level.
